findings.F1: The Calmar fails because of one long fall. The book's deepest fall is 56.8 % and runs over 1215 days from w1 to w11. Holding the coins lost 43.2 % over the same stretch. Against that fall, the book's yearly return of 32.6 % gives a Calmar of 0.57.
findings.F2: The book's gain sits almost entirely in the later windows. In w11 to w24 the 1405 cases have an unusual 5-day move of +1.00 %, and the positions' summed hourly gain is 19.0. In w1 to w10 the 983 cases have −0.59 %, and the summed gain is only 1.35, even though exposure there is higher (0.65 against 0.56) while the coins' summed log return is −5.76.
findings.F3: The cases lose in the coins' bear years. The unusual move is −1.02 % in 2018 (285 cases) and −1.49 % in 2022 (312 cases). It is +2.74 % in 2020 and +1.18 % in 2021.
findings.F4: In w1 to w10, surges that come while the 30-day high has risen over the past week are followed by falls. These 206 cases have an unusual move of −1.79 % (t −2.83). Cases with a falling 30-day high in the same windows have +0.54 %.
findings.F5: The effect is not graded by the size of the surge. Cases split by the 24-hour return in usual daily moves all have unusual moves between +0.25 % and +0.41 % (t below 0.9). The highest 24-hour-return quarter even has the worst average drawdown inside the hold (−8.7 %) and the most losses beyond 10 % (14.6 %).
findings.F6: The effect is concentrated at the very top of the 30-day range. Cases in the top 9 % of the range (545 cases) have an unusual move of +1.44 % (t 2.24). The other three quarters have −0.06 % to +0.32 %.
findings.F7: A stop would not save the book. After the first 24 hours, the fifth of cases that fell most on their first day (below −2.9 %) still rise +0.73 % over the next 4 days (t 1.4). So the falls come from long bear spans, not from surges that fail at once.
findings.F8: The idea is small but its trades pay. The unusual move is +0.38 % per case, 0.036 of the coin's usual 5-day move, which is 1.9 times the 0.19 % round-trip cost. The total move is +1.02 %, 5.3 times the cost. The book clears its costs; what it lacks is protection from the coins' shared bear spans.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, first reaches several times its 30-day average absolute daily return on the upside, the price keeps rising over the next 5 days by more than the coin's usual 5-day return, only while the close stands near its 30-day high and the coin's 1-year return is positive: the closer the close to its 30-day high and the larger its 1-year return at that hour, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would take near-high surges only inside a coin's year-long uptrend, and refuse them during multi-month bear markets, where the book's deepest fall was made.
ideas.name: surge near high, yearly uptrend

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, first reaches several times its 30-day average absolute daily return on the upside, the price keeps rising over the next 5 days by more than the coin's usual 5-day return, only while the close stands in the top of its 30-day range: the higher the close within its 30-day low-to-high range at that hour, the larger the rise, whatever the size of the surge.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size the surge by where it leaves the close in the month's range, not by how large the surge was, and would refuse surges that end below the month's top.
ideas.name: surge at top of range
